name: Chondrocyte (cartilage cell)
short_description: Round to ovoid cell sitting alone or in small isogenous groups inside a matrix-carved lacuna; rich rough ER and Golgi for producing/maintaining the collagen-II and proteoglycan cartilage matrix around it. Cartilage is avascular, so chondrocytes rely on diffusion and store glycogen/lipid as energy reserve.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; single round-to-oval cell in a wavy-walled lacuna surrounded by a pale fibrous matrix halo, eccentric nucleus with prominent nucleolus, extensive folded rough ER, curved perinuclear Golgi stack, several mitochondria, glycogen/lipid inclusions, fine intermediate-filament cytoskeleton mesh; muted desaturated palette with thin clean outlines matching the house textbook style; no blood vessels, no elongated body, no baked text or border)
